description.text: Inspection, measurement, sampling, marking, and record tasks of quality control inspector 51-9061.00; checks the US SOC 51-9061 combined-occupation wage percentiles and the 2025—2035 projection, the Chinese evidence gap, entry paths, and paper inspection exercises that can be completed independently.

subject.name: Quality control inspector
subject.summary: Quality control inspectors turn drawings, specifications, and sampling requirements into repeatable inspection steps, check raw materials, parts, or finished products with measuring instruments and test equipment such as calipers, micrometers, and gauges, mark accept or reject status, record inspection data, and report non-conformances and exceptions; the core responsibility is to make the decision traceable, not just to "find fault". This page uses the US O*NET-SOC 51-9061.00 (Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers) as a transparent proxy: the current O*NET release has no detailed occupation record named Quality Control Inspectors, so the US wages and employment use the SOC 51-9061 combined-occupation basis rather than a narrower single-occupation value, and the two cannot be substituted for each other. No verifiable wage for the detailed occupation was obtained for China, and an insufficient evidence marker is retained.
